hints: Notice that crotyl alcohol has two different functional groups, so ask yourself which group each reagent attacks first.

Remember that $\text{Br}_2$ adds across a $\text{C=C}$ double bond, while strong oxidisers like $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7/\text{H}^+$ and concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4/\text{H}^+$ do more than just oxidise the $\text{-OH}$ group.
Think about which reagent simply swaps $\text{-OH}$ for $\text{-Cl}$ and leaves the $\text{C=C}$ untouched at room temperature.
walkthrough:
**Spot the two functional groups**

Crotyl alcohol is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{OH}$. It has an alkene $\text{C=C}$ and a primary alcohol $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$. Any reagent could react at either site, so we must check both.

Structure idea:
$$\text{CH}_3-\text{CH=CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Recall what each reagent does**

$\text{Br}_2$ at room temperature does electrophilic addition to $\text{C=C}$ to give a dibromo compound. $\text{PCl}_5$ at room temperature substitutes $\text{-OH}$ by $\text{-Cl}$ and leaves $\text{C=C}$ alone.

Key reactions:
$$\text{C=C} + \text{Br}_2 \rightarrow \text{C(Br)-C(Br)}$$
$$\text{R-OH} + \text{PCl}_5 \rightarrow \text{R-Cl} + \text{POCl}_3 + \text{HCl}$$

**Compare mild and strong oxidation**

With $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7/\text{H}^+$ heated under reflux, a primary alcohol goes all the way to a carboxylic acid, not stopping at the aldehyde. With concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4/\text{H}^+$ heated under reflux, oxidation is even more vigorous and cleaves the $\text{C=C}$ bond completely.

Oxidation ladder:
$$\text{RCH}_2\text{OH} \rightarrow \text{RCHO} \rightarrow \text{RCO}_2\text{H}$$
$$\text{C=C} \xrightarrow{\text{conc. KMnO}_4/\text{H}^+, \text{heat}} \text{cleavage to acids / ketones / CO}_2$$

**Pick the only consistent row**

Only the $\text{PCl}_5$ row leaves the double bond intact and correctly gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{Cl}$. All other rows ignore addition to the alkene, stop oxidation too early, or ignore cleavage of the alkene.

options.A: Incorrect. $\text{Br}_2$ does not substitute $\text{-OH}$ by $\text{-Br}$ here. At room temperature it adds across the $\text{C=C}$ bond to give $\text{CH}_3\text{CHBrCHBrCH}_2\text{OH}$. The $\text{C=C}$ would disappear, so $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{Br}$ cannot be the main product.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{K}_2\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7/\text{H}^+$ heated under reflux oxidises a primary alcohol fully to the carboxylic acid, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$. The aldehyde $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCHO}$ would only be the main product with distillation to remove it immediately, not reflux.
options.C: Incorrect. Concentrated $\text{KMnO}_4/\text{H}^+$ under reflux is a very strong oxidiser. It oxidises the $\text{-CH}_2\text{OH}$ group but also cleaves the $\text{C=C}$ bond to give smaller fragments such as ethanoic acid and $\text{CO}_2$. The intact alkene acid $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCO}_2\text{H}$ will not survive.
options.D: Correct. $\text{PCl}_5$ at room temperature converts alcohols to chloroalkanes by nucleophilic substitution of $\text{-OH}$ by $\text{-Cl}$. It does not attack the $\text{C=C}$ bond, so $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{OH}$ cleanly gives $\text{CH}_3\text{CH=CHCH}_2\text{Cl}$.
